JusPrin makes advanced 3D printing feel immediate: a confident path from model to machine that removes detours without hiding control. It is a dense, native desktop application for Windows, macOS and Linux, with a chat Agent beside the 3D workspace. Build every surface to feel focused, assured, inventive and approachable.

## Voice and name

- Write the name exactly as **JusPrin**: capital J and P, no space, never all caps in body copy. Set it in the surrounding text colour; never put the gradient on small text.
- Be direct, capable and optimistic. Never cute, cryptic or over-engineered.
- Prefer plain language to slicer jargon. Say "Slice plate", not "Generate G-code".
- Make the next action obvious. One `ButtonPrimary` per view names the thing the screen is for; everything else is quieter.
- Buttons and labels are sentence case, verb first, with no full stop: "Add printer", "Open printer settings", "Undo".
- Address the person as "you". The Agent speaks as "I". No emoji anywhere in the product.
- A status is never colour alone: pair the colour with an icon and a plain-language label, such as a `circle-alert` glyph beside "Printer offline".

## Logo

- Use the files in `assets/Logos` as they are. Do not stretch, rotate, redraw, recolour, outline, shadow or take the mark apart.
- Default to `jusprin-mark.svg` for application icons and small product contexts, and to the horizontal lockup when there is room for the name.
- Place the logo only on `neutral-white`, `neutral-mist`, `neutral-ink` or another quiet solid field, never over an image or pattern.
- Keep clear space of at least a quarter of the mark's width on every side.
- Minimum sizes on screen: 24px for the mark, 120px wide for the horizontal lockup. Below that, use the mark alone.
- Use the single-ink marks only when the gradient cannot be shown: `jusprin-mark-ink.svg` on light grounds, `jusprin-mark-white.svg` on dark ones.

## Colour

- Style product UI with the semantic tokens (`surface-*`, `text-*`, `border-*`, `action-*`, `status-*`). The primitives (`brand-*`, `neutral-*`) are the palette behind them, for brand artwork and covers, not a component API. The one exception is `Tooltip`, which is `neutral-ink` with `neutral-white` text in both modes.
- Page background is `surface-canvas`. Sidebars and grouped settings sit on `surface-subtle`. Dialogs, menus and popovers sit on `surface-raised` with an elevation shadow. A highlighted row inside them (hover or keyboard focus) is filled with `surface-raised-hover`, not `surface-subtle`, which would look sunk in on a dark menu.
- Body copy and values are `text-primary`; descriptions are `text-secondary`; metadata and placeholders are `text-tertiary`.
- `action-primary` is for the decisive action, the selected segment and text links. It is Orbit purple in light mode and Bloom pink in dark mode, so always put `action-on-primary` on it, never a literal white.
- Dark mode is a remapping of the same token names, not an inversion. Keep hierarchy, density and geometry identical and let the tokens change the values.
- The signature gradient runs from `brand-orbit` to `brand-bloom`. Reserve it for the logo, the splash screen, onboarding and rare hero moments. Never use it as ordinary product chrome.
- `axis-x`, `axis-y` and `axis-z` belong to the 3D viewport only. Never use them for status.
- A failed print or task is reported on `surface-failure-inverse`, a dark panel in both modes, with the `text-on-failure-*`, `status-danger-on-inverse` and `border-on-failure` tokens. Do not mix the ordinary text tokens onto it.

## Typography

- One family for all product UI: HarmonyOS Sans SC in Regular (400) and Bold (700), with the system UI font as fallback. There are no other weights and no italics.
- Use the ten type styles as they are and pick the nearest one; never set a bespoke size. `page-title` 24/30, `section` 18/24, `body` 14/20, `body-small` 13/18, `label` 12/16, `metadata` 10/14, each with a bold partner.
- The Agent conversation is read at `body`: messages, reply choices, the message box, and the text of the cards in the thread. Buttons are not: `ButtonSecondary` is `body-small` at 32px and `ButtonPrimary` `body-small-bold` at 34px everywhere, the buttons of the cards in the thread included. What supports it sits one step below: `body-small` for card details, notes from JusPrin and the setup card's lines, `label-bold` for small card headings and the setup card's eyebrow. The turn's activity line and timestamps are `metadata`. The chat list, the chat header and the message box's pickers keep their own sizes.
- Bold is for emphasis inside a run of the same size: the primary action beside secondary ones, the current row of a menu, a chip's name beside its detail.
- `code` (12/16, the system monospace font) is only for code, keys, file paths, commands and IDs. Names, words, numbers and measurements stay in the sans face; its digits are already equal width, so changing values do not shift.
- Letter spacing is 0 everywhere. Capitals are reserved for short eyebrow captions set in `metadata-bold`, such as "CURRENT SETUP", "STEP 1 OF 3" and menu section titles; type them in capitals rather than transforming the text.

## Layout and geometry

- Whole-screen structure (top bar, panes, where menus open) is in the Application layout section. Every screen is a board on the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ), and the board is the screen's specification. The layer-by-layer files copied from the Figma file are kept as history under `archived/screens/`; do not build from them.
- Design for a dense desktop application measured in device-independent pixels. Do not import web habits: no oversized controls, blur, glass or hero spacing inside the application shell.
- Space with the scale only: `space-4`, `space-8`, `space-12`, `space-16`, `space-20`, `space-24`, `space-32`, `space-40`, `space-48`.
- Controls take `radius-small` (4px). Containers such as cards, popovers and chat bubbles take `radius-medium` (8px), and so does `ButtonPrimary`, the one branded action. `ChatReplyChoice` is the one capsule control (`radius-full`): it is a reply the person could send, so it takes the person's bubble colour and a shape no app control uses. Sheets and large dialogs take `radius-large` (12px). Radii of 16px and above are for onboarding and marketing only.
- Borders are 1px `border-subtle`, drawn inside the box so a bordered control keeps its stated height.
- Control heights are compact, and each is a token: 26px for fields, selects and text links (`component-field-height`, `component-select-height`, `component-buttonLink-height`), 28px for chips and reply choices (`component-chip-height`, `component-replyChip-height`), 30px for a segmented control (`component-segmented-height`), 32px for a secondary or icon button (`component-buttonSecondary-height`, `component-buttonIcon-size`), 34px for a primary or split button (`component-buttonPrimary-height`, `component-buttonSplit-height`), 28px for the compact Send and Stop buttons beside the message box (`component-buttonPrimarySmall-height`, `component-buttonSecondarySmall-height`), 36px for a menu row (`component-menuRow-height`).
- Shadows mark elevation, not decoration: `elevation-subtle` for tooltips, `elevation-medium` for menus and popovers, `elevation-strong` for sheets and dialogs. Flat surfaces carry no shadow.
- Every progress track is `component-progress-height` (4px) thick.

## Iconography

- Functional icons are Lucide 1.47.0 outlines, kept unchanged in `assets/Icons`. Inline the SVG and colour it with the surrounding text token through `currentColor`.
- Draw icons at 16, 20 or 24px. The only exception is the 14px fact glyph inside the setup card (`component-setupCard-iconSize`).
- Keep the JusPrin mark and product-specific symbols custom; do not approximate them with Lucide glyphs, and do not decorate with logo-derived shapes where a functional icon is clearer.
- No emoji and no filled icon sets.

## Components and states

- Every interactive component defines normal, hover, pressed, disabled and keyboard-focus states, plus success, warning and error where they apply.
- Hover and pressed change the fill, not the size: quiet controls go to `surface-subtle` then `surface-selected`; the primary action goes to `action-primary-hover` then `action-primary-pressed`.
- Fields show state on their stroke: 1px `border-subtle` at rest, `border-strong` on hover, 2px `border-focus` when focused, 1px `status-danger` with a message when wrong, and an `action-disabled` fill when disabled.
- Disabled controls keep their shape. Filled and icon buttons drop to 40% opacity, outlined buttons to 50%; fields, selects and chips switch to `action-disabled` and `action-disabled-text`. Do not hide a disabled action.
- Actions: `ButtonPrimary` once per view, `ButtonSecondary` for other labelled actions, `ButtonIcon` when a glyph alone is unmistakable, `ButtonLink` for low-emphasis moves such as "‹ Back" and "Undo", and `ButtonSplit` when the main action has alternatives.
- Entry: `FieldText`, `FieldSecret` for codes and keys, `FieldSearch` to filter a list, `FieldNumber` for one parameter, `FieldVerificationCode` for a six-digit code. Choice: `SegmentedControl` for two to five short options, `Select` for more, `Checkbox` for on or off, `Swatch` for a filament colour.
- Menus are a `MenuPopover` of `MenuRow`s, grouped with `MenuSectionTitle`. Focused tasks sit in a `Sheet`; an action that cannot be undone asks first with `DialogConfirmation`.
- Canvas tools use a `ToolPanel` of `FormRow`s. Status is shown with `StatusDot` and `Progress`, always beside words. `Stepper` marks position in a short setup sequence; `Tooltip` names icon-only controls; `DisclosureTechnicalDetails` folds away secondary detail.
- The Agent pane is built from `ChatHeader`, `PinnedSetupCard`, `ChatBubble`, `ChatReplyChoice`, `ChatAttachment`, `ChatTurnActivity`, `ChatToolActivity` and `Composer`. The header carries `ChipPrinterSpool`; the Home screen lists `ProjectCard`s and `PrinterCard`s.
- Draw every glyph with `Icon`.
- The six coded compositions, `PinnedSetupCard`, `ChatHeader`, `Composer`, `ChipPrinterSpool`, `PrinterCard` and `ProjectCard`, stay coded here. Their drawn source of truth and their variants are the boards on the Compositions page of the JusPrin v2 canvas, and a change to one starts there.
- `ChatSystemLine`, `NoticeStrip`, `CodeBlock`, `DiffBlock` and `ToolStrip` are static renditions: drawn on the canvas, copied here as drawn, and not coded.

## Accessibility

- Text meets 4.5:1 on the surface its token names; large text, control boundaries that carry meaning, icons and focus rings meet 3:1.
- Keyboard focus is a visible 2px `border-focus` ring, offset 2px. Never signal focus with a fill change alone.
- `status-warning` is the one exception in light mode, at about 2.5:1 on `surface-canvas`: use it for the warning glyph only, beside a `text-primary` label.
- `border-subtle` is decorative. A control must be recognisable by its label or glyph without it.

## Not synced

This design system and the JusPrin v2 canvas are the up-to-date JusPrin design. They began on 2026-10-13 as copies of a Figma file; since 2026-10-20 Figma is retired and out of date, and changes are made here directly. The font files cover Latin only; Chinese, Korean and Thai text falls back to the system font. `code` is the system monospace stack the application ships. Each component card shows its variants in light and in dark; where no dark variant is drawn, the dark panel is the light variant with the Dark values of the same tokens. Photographs and 3D renders appear as flat placeholders, and artwork larger than 64px is not drawn. The Agent cards are drawn on the canvas but are not built as coded components, and the five static renditions are copies of their canvas drawings.

content.text:
Yes, I can. I've drawn six logo concepts as vector shapes on a design canvas: https://claude.ai/artifact/Qroq8EdcQDSPkCAyFceDtQ

The first board puts all six side by side. Each concept then has its own board with:
- the mark at large size
- the mark beside "JusPrin" on a light background and on a dark one
- a rounded app icon
- the mark at 48, 32 and 24 px, so you can check it still reads at icon size

They all use your Orbit purple to Bloom pink gradient and the HarmonyOS Sans Bold font from your design system. The shapes are all new.

1. **Nozzle buddy**: a printer nozzle drawn as a little character with two eyes. A small sparkle drips out of the tip. It's the most playful of the six.
2. **Layer J**: a "J" built from stacked rounded bars, like print layers. The top layer is still being laid down, with a dot where the nozzle is.
3. **Spark drop**: a drop of melted filament with a four-point sparkle cut out of the middle. It's the cleanest and most "modern tech" one, and the sparkle carries over from your current star.
4. **Print chat**: a speech bubble whose lines are print layers, and the last layer is still being printed. It says "a printer you talk to", which is the core of the product.
5. **Happy cube**: a smiling cube drawn at an angle, with layer lines on one side and a sparkle on top. It uses three flat brand colours instead of the gradient.
6. **Filament J**: one thick stroke of filament bent into a "J", with a sparkle beside it.

My pick for modern but fun is **Print chat** or **Spark drop**. Both stay clear at 24 px. Nozzle buddy is the most fun, but its eyes get hard to see below about 32 px.

Before any of these can replace the current logo:
- **Not exported yet.** The marks exist only on the canvas. Once you pick one, I'll tune it and export clean `.svg` files in the same set you have today in `resources/jusprin/branding/`: gradient, ink-only and white-only versions, plus a version with the name.
- **Design system rules need updating.** Your design system says to use the existing logo files unchanged, so its logo files and that rule need updating along with the app.
- **The canvas is private.** Others can't open the link until you share it from the page's Share menu.

content.text:
I've added six new versions of the layered J to the canvas: https://claude.ai/artifact/Qroq8EdcQDSPkCAyFceDtQ

They're in a new section headed "Layered J, maker and open-source directions", below the first six concepts. As before, there's an overview board first, then one board per version. Each board shows the mark large, with the JusPrin name on light and dark backgrounds, as an app icon, and at 48, 32 and 24 px.

Each version borrows a familiar maker or open-source idea, drawn fresh rather than copied from any real logo:

- **Gear J**: the layered J sits inside a gear with rounded teeth. Gears are the usual symbol for open-source hardware and for makers in general.
- **Bead J**: the J is built from round dots on a grid instead of bars. It looks like the beads of plastic a printer lays down, or the LED dot displays on maker boards. The last dot is smaller, as if it's still being printed.
- **Perimeter J**: the J is drawn as two outlines inside each other, the way a slicer preview shows a part's walls. This is the most "slicer" of the six.
- **Hex nut J**: a hex nut with the layered J cut out of the middle where the hole would be. It's solid and bold, and holds up best at small sizes.
- **Printing J**: the layered J with a small nozzle hovering over the top layer, printing it. It's the most literal and the most playful.
- **Misprint J**: two copies of the J in purple and pink, slightly out of line, like a hand-printed sticker or zine. It's fun, and it uses two flat brand colours instead of the gradient.

My picks:
- **Hex nut J** if the mark mostly needs to work as an app icon. It's a single solid shape, so it reads clearly at 24 px.
- **Printing J** if you want the most fun and the clearest "3D printing" message. Its nozzle gets very small below 32 px, so the 24 px icon may need a simpler version without it.
- **Gear J and Bead J** are the most obviously maker-flavoured, but both lose detail at 24 px: the gear teeth and the dots start to blur together.

The canvas is still private until you share it from the page's Share menu.

input.recap: The canvas has a third section, "Layered, no letter", with six shapes built from stacked print layers. Each has an overview tile and its own board with the name, dark and app-icon versions, and small sizes. Nothing is exported as SVG files yet.
input.ask: Which layered idea should I take further?

content.text:
I've added six layered ideas with no letter to the canvas: https://claude.ai/artifact/Qroq8EdcQDSPkCAyFceDtQ

They're in a new section headed "Layered, no letter", below the two earlier sets. As before, there's an overview board first and then one board per idea. Each board shows the mark large, with the JusPrin name on light and dark backgrounds, as an app icon, and at 48, 32 and 24 px.

One correction first: I haven't actually researched maker or open-source logos. Both this round and the last one came from general knowledge of the motifs makers use, like gears, nuts, sliced shapes and print failures, not from studying real logos. If you want ideas grounded in real examples, I can look up a set of real maker and open-source logos and summarise what they have in common.

The six ideas:

- **Shifted orb**: a circle sliced into horizontal print layers, with one layer slipped sideways. A shifted layer is a print failure every maker recognises, so it's a wink at a slicer that fixes failed prints. It's simple, modern and holds up at small sizes.
- **Printing dome**: a dome of layers getting wider toward the bottom, with a small nozzle laying down the top layer. It's the most literal "3D printing" picture.
- **Twist from above**: five rounded squares inside each other, each turned a little more, like a twisted vase seen from the top. It's the most abstract and elegant one. The thin lines blur below 32 px.
- **Layered vase**: thin layers whose widths trace a vase's outline, the classic first print people show off. It's calm and refined rather than funny.
- **Layer buddy**: a rounded stack of layers with eyes, a smile and a small sparkle on top. It's the most fun, and it reads like a friendly mascot for the in-app helper.
- **Stringing stack**: a neat block of layers where the top one trails off into a curly loose strand. Stringing, where thin plastic threads trail between parts of a print, is another failure makers joke about.

My picks:
- **Shifted orb** for modern but fun. It's one clean shape, it works at 24 px, and the shifted layer gives it a joke that makers will get.
- **Layer buddy** if you'd rather lean further into fun.

The canvas is still private until you share it from its Share menu.

input.recap: The canvas has a fourth section, "Fun layered ideas", with six playful objects built from print layers. Each has an overview tile and its own board with the name, dark and app-icon versions, and small sizes. Nothing is exported as SVG files yet.
input.ask: Which fun layered idea should I take further?

content.text:
I've added six fun layered ideas to the canvas: https://claude.ai/artifact/Qroq8EdcQDSPkCAyFceDtQ

They're in a fourth section headed "Fun layered ideas", below the earlier sets. As before, there's an overview board first and then one board per idea. Each board shows the mark large, with the JusPrin name on light and dark backgrounds, as an app icon, and at 48, 32 and 24 px.

Each one is a familiar, cheerful object made of stacked print layers:

- **Soft serve**: a swirl of ice cream in a waffle cone, with a curl on top. A soft-serve machine squeezes out the swirl in stacked rings, much as a 3D printer lays down plastic. It's friendly and instantly readable, and it's my favourite of this set.
- **Layer cake**: a birthday cake of print layers with dripping icing and one candle, whose flame is the sparkle from your current logo. It's celebratory, like a successful print.
- **Wobbly tower**: a block-stacking tower with one block pulled halfway out and the top block slightly tilted. Its message is "careful building", with a bit of suspense.
- **Spaghetti stack**: three tidy layers with a tangle of loose plastic above them. "Spaghetti" is the best-known failed-print joke among makers. It also suits a slicer that fixes failed prints, and Obico's past as The Spaghetti Detective.
- **Layer rocket**: a rocket built from layers, with a round window, two fins and a flame. Its message is "launch your print".
- **Layer castle**: a sandcastle-style castle of layers with battlements, an arched door and a flag. Its message is "build something".

My picks:
- **Soft serve** is the strongest idea. The link between soft serve and printing is easy to get, and the shape stays clear at 32 px. The waffle lines on the cone disappear at 24 px, so a small-size version would drop them.
- **Spaghetti stack** has the best story for your users and your history, but the tangle looks messy at small sizes. It would work better as a mascot or illustration than as the app icon.
- **Layer cake** and **Layer castle** both hold up well at small sizes.

The canvas is still private until you share it from its Share menu.

# Resource overlay

Files here replace the OrcaSlicer resource of the same name at runtime.
`Slic3r::var()` checks `overlay/images/` before `resources/images/`, so an
upstream call such as `ScalableBitmap(this, "OrcaSlicer_about", 125)` renders
the JusPrin artwork without any edit to the calling code. Keep the OrcaSlicer
file names; they are the lookup keys. An SVG here shadows an upstream PNG of
the same stem because the bitmap loaders try SVG first.

Current overlays: splash, About lockup, horizontal lockup, monochrome mark
(message dialogs), setup-wizard watermark, and the window icon PNGs.
----
# JusPrin resources

This directory contains curated, production-facing JusPrin assets. Generated decks, PDFs, render trees, archives, inspection output, and design-tool working directories remain on `jusprin-v2-poc` and are indexed in `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md`.

- `branding/` contains the original gradient mark and approved monochrome variants.
- `ui/` contains the authoritative semantic product UI tokens, `design-tokens.json`, which the shell, the Agent page, and `tests/brand/` all read.
- `images/` contains the application icons the bundle and installer reference directly (`JusPrin.icns`, `JusPrin.ico`).
- `overlay/images/` contains the splash, About and horizontal lockups, monochrome mark, wizard watermark, and window icon PNGs under OrcaSlicer's asset names; `Slic3r::var()` serves them in place of the stock files. Lockups are generated from `branding/jusprin-mark.svg` plus the JusPrin wordmark set in HarmonyOS Sans SC Bold, so they render through nanosvg without a text element.

The original logo was supplied by the user and restored from repository revision `6eecb78b19`. Do not redraw, separate, rotate, stretch, or arbitrarily recolor it.

    gpos=f['GPOS'].table; tot=0

        for st in lk.SubTable:
            if lk.LookupType==9: st=st.ExtSubTable
            if getattr(st,'LookupType',lk.LookupType)!=2: continue

            if st.Format==1:

content.text:
I added the layered name to the logo canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/Qroq8EdcQDSPkCAyFceDtQ), in a new section at the bottom called "Soft serve with a layered name". I haven't looked at how the boards render, and no logo files in the repo have been changed.

The first board shows five ways to draw the name next to the cone, each on a light and a dark background:

- **A, sliced name.** I turned the app's own bold font into vector outlines and cut it into print layers, with the same gap-to-layer ratio as the cone. Capital letters are seven layers tall and small letters five, so every letter's top lands on a whole layer.
- **B, sliced name in the gradient.** This is A filled with the purple-to-pink logo gradient. The design system keeps that gradient off text, so this one breaks its rule. I only drew it on light.
- **C, printing the dot.** This is A with a small print nozzle above the i, as if the dot is the last layer still being printed. It's the most playful of the five, and the name still reads normally.
- **D, name built from bars.** Every letter is made of the same rounded bars as the cone, so the name and the cone match exactly. It reads more like a pixel font than the others.
- **E, stacked.** The cone sits above the sliced name, for square spaces like the splash screen.

The second board shows A, C and D with the cone 48, 32 and 24 px tall. That's where layered text tends to break down: at 24 px each layer is about 1.5 px thick. For a header-sized logo, I expect the layers to turn grey and blurry unless the small version uses the plain name.

Once you pick a style, I'll do the swap using the file list you approved.

# Resource overlay

Files here replace the OrcaSlicer resource of the same name at runtime.
`Slic3r::var()` checks `overlay/images/` before `resources/images/`, so an
upstream call such as `ScalableBitmap(this, "OrcaSlicer_about", 125)` renders
the JusPrin artwork without any edit to the calling code. Keep the OrcaSlicer
file names; they are the lookup keys. An SVG here shadows an upstream PNG of
the same stem because the bitmap loaders try SVG first.

Current overlays: splash, About lockup, horizontal lockup, monochrome mark
(message dialogs), setup-wizard watermark, and the window icon PNGs.
# JusPrin resources

This directory contains curated, production-facing JusPrin assets. Generated decks, PDFs, render trees, archives, inspection output, and design-tool working directories remain on `jusprin-v2-poc` and are indexed in `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md`.

- `branding/` contains the original gradient mark and approved monochrome variants.
- `ui/` contains the authoritative semantic product UI tokens, `design-tokens.json`, which the shell, the Agent page, and `tests/brand/` all read.
- `images/` contains the application icons the bundle and installer reference directly (`JusPrin.icns`, `JusPrin.ico`).
- `overlay/images/` contains the splash, About and horizontal lockups, monochrome mark, wizard watermark, and window icon PNGs under OrcaSlicer's asset names; `Slic3r::var()` serves them in place of the stock files. Lockups are generated from `branding/jusprin-mark.svg` plus the JusPrin wordmark set in HarmonyOS Sans SC Bold, so they render through nanosvg without a text element.

The original logo was supplied by the user and restored from repository revision `6eecb78b19`. Do not redraw, separate, rotate, stretch, or arbitrarily recolor it.

"""Build JusPrin translation catalogs from OrcaSlicer's .po files.

OrcaSlicer names itself in about 85 user-facing strings and in every
translation of them. Rather than editing those source strings (and the
translation macros) in upstream files, this script produces the catalogs the
application loads, with the product name substituted:

    msgstr is empty but whose msgid names the product get the substituted
    English text so the fallback also reads correctly;

The .mo writer is self-contained so the build does not need gettext.

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.

- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The name on that row was also pushed down, so its top layers were cut off and it read "IusDrin". The cone now shows in full on every row, and the "Printing the dot" row shows the whole name with the nozzle above the i, on both light and dark. The small-size board had the same bug and is fixed too.

**The repo logo files.** Before your message I had already drawn the new logo files for the app. They are built a different way, so this bug doesn't affect them. I rendered every one with nanosvg, the SVG renderer the app uses, and they draw correctly with the gradient and the cone's waffle cut-outs.

The changes are in a separate worktree on branch `claude/new-logo`, made from `jusprin-newui`. Nothing is committed. They cover:

- **Source marks:** the three files in `resources/jusprin/branding/` (gradient, ink and white).
- **App icons:** `JusPrin.icns`, `JusPrin.ico` and the Linux `JusPrin.png`. They use the same light tile as the current icon, with the gradient cone on it.
- **In-app images:** splash, About, horizontal lockup, grey mark, setup-wizard watermark and window icons. Each keeps its old canvas size.
- **Two new overlay files** that replace OrcaSlicer's whale:
  - `OrcaSlicer.svg`, used by message, release-note and update dialogs.
  - `OrcaSlicer-mac_256px.ico`, the Mac Dock icon.
- **A script,** `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Brand/brand_logo.py`, that redraws all of these from one geometry.
- **Docs:** `design-system.md`, `resources/jusprin/README.md` and the overlay README no longer say "never redraw the original logo".

**Not done yet:**

- I haven't seen the logo inside the running app. When I asked for access to a test copy, the request was declined, so I closed that copy.
- Two whale logos still remain:
  - The Send-system-info dialog reads its file by full path, which skips the overlay.

  Covering either one means editing an OrcaSlicer-owned file, so I left them alone.
- The design system artifact and the JusPrin v2 screens canvas still show the old logo.

content.text:
I committed the logo swap to `jusprin-newui` in your main checkout as `0cda0677eb`, "Replace the JusPrin logo with the layered soft-serve cone". I made the commit on the logo branch and then moved `jusprin-newui` forward to it, so it sits right on top of `74a0e9b61c`. The branch is one commit ahead of origin, and I haven't pushed.

The commit changes 22 files:
- The three source marks.
- The Mac and Windows app icons, and the Linux AppImage icon.
- The ten in-app logo images.
- Two new files that replace OrcaSlicer's whale: the colour mark used in message, release-note and update dialogs, and the Mac Dock icon.
- The script that draws all of these, `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Brand/brand_logo.py`.
- The three doc updates.

None of OrcaSlicer's own files are edited.

When you test, these are the places to look:
- **Splash screen at startup.** I haven't seen it live, only in nanosvg, the app's SVG renderer.
- **About dialog.** I checked this one in the test app.
- **Dock icon and the app icon in Finder.** I haven't seen these. macOS caches app icons, so you may still see the old one at first; if so, re-copy or rename the .app.
- **A message dialog.** I haven't seen it live either.

Two places will still show the old whale: the send-system-info dialog, and the Linux desktop-integration icon. Both read OrcaSlicer's file directly, so the swap doesn't reach them.

The design system and the v2 canvas still show the old logo. I'll update them once you've decided the new logo is good enough.
